why: A (universe 0) is Morse.isAdInvariant_iff_lieInvariant: for ANY real Lie algebra L and bilinear form B, the project's IsAdInvariant B (⟨[X,Y],Z⟩ = ⟨X,[Y,Z]⟩) ↔ Mathlib's B.lieInvariant; IsAdInvariant and IsLeviCivita (torsion D X Y − D Y X = ⁅X,Y⁆ and B (D X Y) Z + B Y (D X Z) = 0 for an abstract bilinear D on L) are vocabulary — the project never passes from a Lie group to its algebra. B: for a Lie group G (Mathlib LieGroup, ℝⁿ model) with a bi-invariant metric and a Levi-Civita connection, six facts on 𝔤 = GroupLieAlgebra: (1) [X_u,X_v] = X_⁅u,v⁆, (2) ⟨X_u,X_v⟩ ≡ ⟨u,v⟩, (3) X_u ⊢ X_v is left-invariant, (4) torsion, (5) metric compatibility on 𝔤, (6) 21.3(a). B ⇒ A only vacuously (A re-proved in 4 lines). A ⇒ B fails: A has no group. Dictionary proved (#rt_check OK): (1), (2), (4) hold outright (Mathlib mulInvariantVector_mlieBracket; left invariance; IsSymm at 1 with C^∞ of left-invariant fields, isSmoothVF_liv, re-done for ∞ since Mathlib only gives C²); (4)∧(5) ↔ Morse.IsLeviCivita ipForm (connAt cov 1 id) exactly (ipForm = metric at 1 as a BilinForm, connAt = (u,v) ↦ (X_u ⊢ X_v)(1), bilinear via Mathlib's CovariantDerivative additivity); (6) ↔ IsAdInvariant ipForm ↔ (by A) ipForm.lieInvariant. So B ↔ (3)∧(5)∧(6) (B_iff_geometric_core): the remaining content is genuine geometry absent from the project — left-invariance of ∇ on 𝔤, the derivative form of compatibility from the blind parallel-transport definition, and 21.3(a) itself (needs X ⊢ X = 0).
overlap: B_to_A: 1 shared [Morse.IsAdInvariant._proof_1] (auxiliary proof inside the definition; the re-proof is Lie skew-symmetry). Bridges B6_iff_lieInvariant and B_iff_geometric_core also pass #rt_check.
